name: Haikou Meilan International Airport
before:
Hainan's largest and busiest airport, 25 km south east of Haikou, handling 26,851,102 passengers in 2025 and ranking 20th among China's civil airports.

The terminal split matters. Terminal 2 handles all international flights as well as most China Southern and Hainan domestic services, with check-in islands A and B reserved for international departures. Terminal 1 takes the remaining domestic flights. The old separate International Terminal closed on 7 February 2023 when new immigration facilities opened in Terminal 2, so any guidance pointing at it is out of date.

Terminal 2 has four levels and international departures clear immigration on the fourth, which is worth knowing when a client is looking for the right floor.

The runway is 3,600 metres with a Category II instrument approach on runway 09.

The airport opened in 1999, replacing the old Dayingshan Airport.
after:
Hainan's busiest airport, 25 km south east of Haikou, handling 26.9 million passengers in 2025 and ranking 20th among China's airports.

The terminal split matters. Terminal 2, opened in December 2021, handles all international flights as well as Hainan Airlines and China Southern; Terminal 1 takes the remaining domestic flights. International passengers moved from the old separate International Terminal to Terminal 2 in February 2023, so any guidance pointing at it is out of date.

International departures check in at island A on the third floor of Terminal 2 and clear immigration on the fourth.

There are two runways, each 3,600 metres long.
